walkthroughs.body_html: A railroad iron bar shot through Gage's frontal lobe. He survived but became impulsive, rude and unreliable — 'no longer Gage'. The case supported the idea that personality and decision-making are localised in the frontal lobe.

HM had his hippocampus removed in 1953 to treat epilepsy. He kept his STM and procedural skills but could no longer form new long-term episodic memories. The case supports separate memory stores and the hippocampus's role in LTM.

Case studies give rich, in-depth data and ethical access to rare conditions. But they involve small samples and may not generalise. They are usually used alongside brain scans (CT, MRI, fMRI) to confirm findings.
